mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificación negativa de denominación social (negative name clearance certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certificate; no apostille required for filing before a Spanish notary and subsequent registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney granted by each foreign corporate shareholder to the local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of the shareholder or a Spanish Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention certificate, unless the origin jurisdiction requires full consular legalization because it is not a party to the Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the foreign shareholder's certificate of incorporation and current registry extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry, ministry of economy, or notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national ID copy and UBO declaration for each ultimate beneficial owner of the Spanish SL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin, embassy/consulate, or Spanish notary for the sworn declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille/legalization for the certified ID copy; the UBO declaration itself is sworn before the Spanish notary executing the deed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory positive identification and verification of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories. Screening must be completed before the incorporation deed is granted against the SEPBLAC risk lists, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list. Enhanced due diligence under Articles 32 and 33 of Law 10/2010 is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates; the screening result must be evidenced in the pre-incorporation compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – Solicitud de certificado de denominación social (online application via www.rmc.es and the electronic headquarters of the Registrars Association of Spain, www.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The chosen name must be written in the Latin script; foreign-language names are permitted when transliterated into Latin characters. Names may include letters, numbers, or their combination, and must end with 'Sociedad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' The name must not be identical to or phonetically or visually confusingly similar to an existing Spanish company or designated public entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Estado, Gobierno, Ministro, Ministerio, Consejo, Instituto Nacional, Ayuntamiento, Universidad, Real
Banco, Caja, Caja de Ahorros, Seguro, Reaseguradora, Mutualidad, Montepío, Pósito, Cooperativa, Sociedad Anónima, S.A., S.A.U., S.Coop.
Cruz Roja, United Nations, Unión Europea, European Central Bank, World Bank, UNESCO, ONCE
Terms contrary to law, public order, or good customs, and terms that may mislead as to the corporate object or the type of company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate automatically expires at the end of the 90-day validity period and no formal extension is available; a fresh application must be submitted for the same or an alternative name. If the Central Commercial Registry rejects a name, the applicant may file a reconsideration submission (recurso de reposición) before the same Registry within 15 working days from notification, addressing the specific grounds of rejection. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may raise the matter before the competent Juzgado de lo Mercantil in accordance with Ley 15/2015, de 2 de julio, de la Jurisdicción Voluntaria.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office can serve as a correspondence and administrative address, but under Article 9 of Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 the statutory registered office must be located in Spain where the effective centre of management or central administration has its actual physical presence. For an ISIC 7420 stock photography and generative visual assets platform operating via Stripe and PayPal, a wholly virtual office is not sufficient to meet the statutory seat test; reliance on a virtual office materially increases the risk of an adverse Spanish tax-residence determination and a commercial substance challenge.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months for a low-risk online stock-media company; the probability increases to approximately 30% if the registered office is a mere virtual address without local staff, records, or hardware, because the authorities may verify the reality of the commercial activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate in Madrid or Barcelona for a virtual office bundle with mail handling

stage_2.agency_name: Consejería competente en medio ambiente de la Comunidad Autónoma de Madrid (Regional Environmental Agency) / Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica for national consistency
stage_2.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA — ISIC 7420 photographic and stock-photo platform services is not listed in Annex I or Annex II of Ley 21/2013 de evaluación ambiental; only a 'memoria ambiental mínima' or declaration ('declaración responsable') may be required for municipal premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria (AEAT) - State Tax Administration Agency; electronic portal: Sede Electronica at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs and excise administered by the AEAT Department of Customs and Excise (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales); annual tax returns filed via Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax), Modelo 303 (VAT), Modelo 036/037 (census registration), and Modelo 349 (recapitulative intra-EU statement).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-owned Spanish SL obtains its statutory Tax ID (NIF) and VAT ID as a single integrated process: (i) execute the notarial deed of incorporation, register the company in the Registro Mercantil, and obtain provisional NIF clearance from AEAT; (ii) file Modelo 036 declaracion censal to request the definitive NIF (8 digits plus control letter), choosing CNAE 7420 photographic activities and declaring the date of commencement - definitive NIF issues within one month, and the same number is the VAT registration number with the prefix 'ES' (e.g., ESB12345674); (iii) non-resident corporate shareholders without a permanent establishment additionally obtain a non-resident NIF (prefix 'N' for foreign corporations) by filing Form 030 with proof of foreign incorporation (apostilled and translated) and appointing a fiscal representative where required for non-EU entities; (iv) foreign entities selling B2C digital services into Spain may bypass local establishment and obtain a Spanish VAT ID through the non-union One-Stop-Shop route. All registration procedures require prior electronic identification by qualified certificate, DNIe, or Cl@ve PIN for submissions through the AEAT portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain follows an opaque entity-level regime; no US-style check-the-box election exists and a Spanish SL is always a taxable person for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) taxed at the standard 25% (15% reduced rate for newly created SLs in the first two profitable tax years subject to turnover and capital conditions, declared via Modelo 036). Available statutory elections include: (i) consolidated tax group regime (arts. 58-70 LIS) for groups with direct or indirect 75% voting control, irrevocable for three years; (ii) patent box election (art. 23 LIS) granting 50% exemption on qualifying IP exploitation income; (iii) ETVE holding-company election giving a territorial exemption for foreign-source dividends and capital gains; (iv) EU ATAD hybrid-mismatch adjustments (art. 15 quaterdecies LIS) which are mandatory rather than elective; (v) for indirect tax, the Union OSS and non-Union OSS elections covering cross-border B2C supply of electronic and stock-photo services. Any election affecting the tax base is filed with the definitive NIF application and updated via Modelo 036 whenever circumstances change.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Anadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 and Real Decreto 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold exists in Spain: any person performing taxable supplies, including digital stock-photo licensing and generative visual-asset sales, must register for VAT from the first euro of turnover. A registration threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year applies only to intra-Community distance and B2C electronic-service sales into other EU Member States (Union OSS threshold); below EUR 10,000 the supply is subject to Spanish 21% VAT. Non-EU service providers selling digital services to Spanish consumers must register for Spanish VAT via the non-union OSS with no local turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance is mandatory through the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Informacion) for large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 6 million), VAT groups, and entities in certain regimes: invoice records G1-G4 must be transmitted electronically to AEAT within 4 calendar days of issue (8 calendar days for third-party issued invoices), using the XSD/TEDE schemas and qualified electronic certificates. The Veri*factu regime (Ley 18/2022 Crea y Crece, RD 1007/2023) obliges all billing software to generate a hash-chain integrity record with timestamps and a QR verification code (codigo VERI); software providers must be compliant by 1 July 2025 and all end-user businesses by 1 January 2026. B2B electronic invoicing in Facturae format is mandated for issuers with turnover above EUR 8 million from 1 July 2025 and for all businesses from 1 January 2026, unless the issuer already reports bills through SII or Veri*factu. Non-compliance blocks VAT refunds and exposes the company to AEAT electronic-settlement penalty rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods to third countries and territories (including Ceuta and Melilla) qualify for the 0% rate (exemption with credit, art. 21.1 LIVA) when the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter holds a validated customs export declaration (DUA). The 0% rate also covers ancillary transport, loading, insurance, and other services directly related to exported goods (art. 21.2 LIVA). For B2B stock-photo licensing, AI-generated visual assets, and digital marketplace services supplied to non-EU business customers, the place of supply is the customer's country (art. 69.1 LIVA); Spanish VAT is not chargeable and the transaction, if still reportable, is captured in Modelo 349 recapitulative returns. B2C digital services to non-EU consumers are placed where the consumer is established or resides (outside the EU) and therefore fall outside Spanish VAT. Zero-rating eligibility requires documentary proof of export or foreign-recipient status rather than mere assertion of non-domicile, and AEAT applies a business-reality test examining substance, pricing, and payment flows.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) with CUSDEC/AAR confirmation and customs officer's exit validation (prueba de exportacion), including 14-digit MRN where applicable
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for sea/air freight, or CMR waybill for road transport, evidencing physical departure from EU territory, with signed proof of delivery (POD) for DDP and DAP terms
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/credit confirmation from the Spanish or EU-acquired banking channel evidencing actual collection of export proceeds

Commercial invoice compliant with RD 1619/2012, containing complete service/goods description, quantity, unit price, INCOTERMS, exemption legenda (Exportacion exenta art. 21 LIVA), and recipient VAT/GST ID

Contractual scope-of-rights documentation for stock-photo and AI-visual licensing (royalty schedules, usage restrictions, territorial grant, and download/revenue evidence from the platform), together with Modelo 349 recapitulative records and, where applicable, the certificate of transferability of the transaction to the platform operator
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audit teams actively target fictitious and inflated export zero-rating schemes, using risk flags such as related-party buyers, cycles through letterbox intermediaries, sales to high-risk territories, pricing outside arm's length range, and funds cleared through PayPal/Stripe without correspondent Spanish banking entry. Consequences of a challenge include: (i) immediate VAT assessment at 21% with statutory late-payment interest, plus the art. 27 LGT surcharge of 1%-20% for late payment; (ii) penalty under art. 191 LGT of 50%-150% of the tax loss, aggravated for intentional conduct; (iii) independent penalty of 50% of the invoice amount (minimum EUR 150) under art. 201 LGT for invoices containing false or misleading data; (iv) fines of EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 per record for omission or incorrect SII/Veri*factu transmission (art. 193 LGT); (v) retrospective clawback of VAT refunds and credit offsets for up to 4 years under the statute of limitations (arts. 66-70 LGT), with unlimited reassessment where the declarant operates through a tax-haven jurisdiction; (vi) criminal referral under art. 305 CP for evasion exceeding EUR 120,000 (imprisonment 2-6 years and fine up to six times the defrauded amount), and under art. 305 bis CP for organized VAT-fraud circuits exceeding EUR 2,000,000 (imprisonment 5-9 years); (vii) removal from the OSS special scheme, revocation of clean-tax certificates, prohibition on public subsidies and concession contracts, and director disqualification for the SL's administrators. Companies using Spanish export zero-rating must therefore retain the full evidentiary bundle for at least the 4-year limitation period and align payment receipt and FX repatriation with the 180-day benchmark to rebut the presumption of fictitious export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks and under the prudential supervision framework of the Single Supervisory Mechanism for euro area credit institutions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a eurozone member state with full liberalization of capital movements under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Spanish Royal Decree-Law 1116/1991 on capital transactions. Current account and capital account convertibility are unrestricted for euro and foreign currency transactions, subject to compliance reporting to the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments Registry for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 or as statutorily required. Dividend and profit remittances by a Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted after corporate tax and withholding tax obligations are satisfied, provided proof of tax residence, beneficial ownership declarations, and anti-money laundering source-of-funds documentation is submitted to the remitting bank. Hurdles are primarily documentary, not exchange control, and include the obligation to file the annual 'Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior' (form C-1) for certain cross-border flows, and the need to present valid tax clearance certificates where required by banking compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists in Spain for euro-denominated receipts or foreign currency receipts. As a eurozone member, Spain has no mandatory conversion ratio or compulsory repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters are, however, required to maintain due documentary support for customs, VAT, and balance of payments declaration purposes and must file the corresponding cross-border transaction declarations with the Bank of Spain when thresholds apply. For stock photo licensing and AI-generated visual asset sales, proceeds received via acquiring platforms (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) are treated as ordinary trade receipts and are freely retained or converted at any licensed bank, subject to standard AML/KYC verification and accurate reflection in the entity's statutory accounting records.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for offshore fintech and Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) is Medium with significant legal constraints. A Spanish SL may open accounts with EU-licensed EMIs operating in Spain under the freedom to provide services or through a Spanish branch; however, such accounts are not a full substitute for a bank account at a credit institution in Spain for purposes of capital increase escrow, trade finance, or certain high-volume payouts. EMIs cannot accept deposits and are not covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund, which elevates counterparty and treasury risk. Offshore non-EU EMIs are generally impractical for primary treasury operations due to Spanish regulatory expectations of a domestic or EU-passported entity, AML equivalence, and the risk of being characterized as unauthorized deposit-taking if structured improperly. Best practice is to use an EMI solely as an auxiliary receivables collection rail while maintaining a primary clearing account with a Tier-1 Spanish commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is generally permitted by Spanish Tier-1 banks for low-risk standard businesses, but the final decision rests with each institution's compliance committee. Beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories must undergo non-face-to-face identity verification using video conferencing or digital certificate validation, supported by notarized corporate documents and apostilled resolutions where required. Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for a low-risk non-resident-owned SL, but many banks require at least one director or authorized representative to attend an in-person interview at a Spanish branch if the compliance score exceeds low-risk thresholds or if the shareholder structure includes complex offshore intermediaries. Foreign directors must present valid passports, proof of address, original or notarized incorporation documents, and a Spanish income tax identification number (NIF) if they will act with fiscal relevance, unless exempted by the bank's internal remote-onboarding policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner with complex shareholding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain chart, certified corporate registers from each jurisdiction, valid passports of all natural-person UBOs, proof of ultimate source of wealth, audited financial statements or independent wealth evidence, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the tiered holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border receivables from distributed online marketplaces (Stripe, PayPal, stock content aggregators)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform service agreements, historical transaction ledgers evidencing genuine commercial activity, VAT registration certificate, ISIC 7420 activity description, customer geolocation breakdown, payout reconciliation reports, and a compliance narrative aligning payment flow origin with the digital content licensing business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Distributed royalty or licensing payouts to foreign content creators and AI generation subcontractors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written licensing agreements, model releases, AI training provenance documentation, subcontractor KYC files, evidence of withholding tax or reverse-charge VAT handling, and a documented business rationale for each cross-border beneficiary to refute money laundering or undisclosed related-party structuring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP-intensive asset base with no physical inventory and low tangible asset footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copyright registrations, digital asset custody records, developer and creator contracts, bank statements demonstrating revenue generation, tax return filings, and board minutes confirming the operational substance of the stock photo AI platform in Spain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections to a Spanish SL must be executed via the Spanish entity's IBAN account at a licensed credit institution, using SWIFT wire with a detailed beneficiary reference. For share capital equity injections, the sender must indicate a payment purpose consistent with the Companies Law and the notarial capital increase if applicable; common references include 'Aportación de capital social', 'Capital increase resolution', or 'Transferencia de fondos propios'. The receiving bank will require the capital increase public deed, the certificate from the Commercial Registry if amounts exceed the ordinary capitalization threshold, and the NIF of the receiving entity. Cross-border funding exceeding EUR 50,000 must be reported to the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments statistical registry, either through the bank's automatic reporting (C-1 form) or via the obligatory declaration. Failing to properly document the purpose code or submit the compliant deed may trigger AML intervention or temporary freezing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for stock photo and generative asset purchases from foreign suppliers, photographer royalties, AI infrastructure vendors, and platform fees should be settled primarily through SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers for non-urgent payments, with correspondent banking fees pre-agreed. Larger or invoice-backed disbursements may be routed via commercial letters of credit (documentary credits) under UCP 600 where the counterparty requires secure delivery against payment; however, for low-risk digital content licensing, MT103 and SEPA instant credit transfers are the standard cost-efficient rails. EUR-denominated payments to EU counterparties should use the SEPA Credit Transfer scheme with mandatory IBAN and BIC validation. Cross-border payments in non-euro currencies require accurate SWIFT message formatting, ISO 20022 compliance, and inclusion of the relevant trade invoice reference to satisfy Spanish foreign transaction reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright press or plain vanilla currency forward contracts against EUR for major convertible currencies (USD, GBP, JPY) executed with a Spanish licensed bank or EU-passported investment firm

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging market currencies where the underlying receivables arise from non-convertible jurisdictions or where settlement cannot be physically executed due to regulatory constraints
Cross-currency interest rate swaps solely for balance sheet hedging of any mapped external debt denominated in a non-euro currency, subject to EMIR clearing and reporting thresholds
FX options (European style) for protecting downside on forecasted USD or GBP income streams while retaining upside participation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (Annual Accounts Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Mercantile Registry) of the company's registered address province
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the shareholders' meeting within 6 months of fiscal year-end (30 June for 31 December year-end); deposit within one month after approval, no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry file closure, denial of future registrations and good-standing certificates until the filing is made; repeated non-deposit may trigger administrative action and potential deregistration after 6 consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax Return, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities, from 1 to 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5% up to 20% of the tax due, plus monthly late-payment interest; omission after official request triggers a fixed fine from €200 and further penalties up to 20% of undeclared amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Titulares Reales (UBO Annual Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (submitted together with annual accounts deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with annual accounts filing, generally by 31 July following the fiscal year end; must also be updated within one month of any UBO change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Infringements of Law 10/2010 attract fines from €600 to €60,000; non-filing also leaves the registry file in a non-compliant status, blocking corporate registrations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 – Declaración Anual de Operaciones con Terceras Personas (Annual Third-Party Transaction Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 20 February for the preceding tax year; filing is required only if cumulative annual transactions with any counterparty exceed €3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of €200 per omitted form plus an additional penalty of up to 0.5% of the undeclared amounts; both capped under the General Tax Law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory if for two consecutive fiscal years the company exceeds at least two of: total assets > €2,846,000; net annual turnover > €5,700,000; average headcount > 50 employees. The audit requirement may also arise due to public-interest status or contractual obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable - PGC) under the Código de Comercio; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts of groups, but individual SL accounts must apply the local PGC, including the micro-entity regime optionality for smaller companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual UBO confirmation requires identifying all shareholders owning more than 25% directly or indirectly, and any control via voting rights or corporate appointments. It is filed jointly with the annual accounts deposit. Shareholding transfers must be recorded in the shareholder register as they occur, and the UBO notification must be revised and submitted to the Mercantile Registry within one month of any reportable change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Accounting Books (Inventory and Daily Ledger, plus Annual Accounts ledger)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% standard rate with R&D tax credits, innovation incentives, and sector-specific reliefs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) via Agencia Tributaria electronic portal (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 days after the end of the fiscal year (e.g. 25 January for calendar-year taxpayers)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before deductions and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents limited to Spanish-source income; certain deductions unavailable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions including tax incentives and loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents restricted to deductions attributable to Spanish-sourced income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax liability after all adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents file only for tax on Spanish-source income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 100 EUR per day late filing (maximum 1,500 EUR); 20-100% surcharge plus interest on unpaid/underpaid tax

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 20,000,000 EUR (net turnover threshold triggering local file)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) require adequate local operations for certain entities and activities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 3 times evaded tax; administrative fines up to 100% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from management roles, and joint liability for tax debts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Comply with Transfer Pricing Rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party transactions without arm's-length documentation or use of non-approved methodologies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines 1,000-5,000 EUR per transaction or 100% of tax advantage; criminal sanctions in aggravated cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and possible imprisonment for fraudulent conduct; directors liable for TP adjustments

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold or remit WHT on dividends, royalties, or interest paid to non-residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 100% of unpaid WHT plus interest; criminal prosecution for willful non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for the tax and penalties; potential jail time for evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Spanish entity without sufficient local operations, employees, or decision-making
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Company dissolution, fines up to 1,000,000 EUR, and potential criminal sanctions under tax and AML laws
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for damages, fines, and criminal charges for fraudulent incorporation or management
